newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss Jew chides WJC boss for missing meeting.
newsitem.headline: Swiss Jew chides WJC boss for missing meeting.

text.p: A prominent Swiss Jew chided World Jewish Congress (WJC) President Edgar Bronfman on Wednesday for missing the first board meeting of a Swiss Holocaust memorial fund and called his absence "a step in the wrong direction".

Bronfman sent WJC secretary general Israel Singer in his place to attend Monday's meeting, which approved the release of an initial 17 million Swiss francs in humanitarian aid to needy Holocaust victims, primarily Jews in eastern Europe.

"After a long fight with hard -- sometimes too hard -- blows, the symbolic value of this absence can unfortunately not be underestimated," Sigmund Feigel, honorary head of Zurich's Jewish community, wrote in a letter faxed to Bronfman.
"I regret to have to ascertain that your personal absence, esteemed Mr President, was a step in the wrong direction," he added. Feigel released a copy in Switzerland.

WJC Executive director Elan Steinberg said in the United States that the press had received Feigel's letter before the WJC did. "Mr Feigel's manner of communication is insulting. His opinions are deemed of no importance by anyone here in the Jewish community, but I wish him a nice day," he added.

The memorial fund administers 170 million Swiss francs in donations from Swiss banks and private businesses eager to burnish neutral Switzerland's humanitarian image amid accusations it cynically profited from World War Two.
The Swiss National Bank, which acknowledges it bought gold during wartime that it should have suspected was looted by the Nazis, also plans to contribute another 100 million francs.
Bronfman is one of three Jewish representatives on the seven-member board, which includes three Swiss representatives and is chaired by Rolf Bloch, a Swiss who heads the country's Jewish federation.
